title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual work but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation and motivate architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so any paired difference is attributable to validation/repair rather than first‑pass prompt or decoding differences.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and preregistration fidelity: completed pairs = 1000, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, repair calls = 5, declared model = gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent inferential reporting: the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (p = 0.0625) is presented as the confirmatory result; the paired bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is presented as a preregistered descriptive summary and explicitly interpreted relative to the confirmatory test.
sections.related_work:
A growing body of work studies LLMs for NetOps, structured outputs, and agentic architectures. Surveys and empirical analyses document hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and failures in code/config generation that motivate validator‑assisted designs [1],[2]. Methods such as schema‑constrained planning and constrained decoding have reduced syntactic or executable errors in several structured domains, though many demonstrations are outside NetOps and benefits depend on constraint tooling and domain fidelity [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers propose verifier‑assisted repair, guarded execution, and governance mechanisms (protocol‑mediated execution, proof carrying) as risk mitigations; these works present prototypes and benchmarked scenarios and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and external governance rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements this literature by preregistering a paired comparison that isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, our estimand measures only downstream effects; it does not evaluate independent first‑pass prompt/decoding interventions that were not executed.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized before any hosted‑model invocation; its SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by both arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Because both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate, the guarded arm cannot benefit from an independent alternative first‑pass generation. Any paired outcome difference can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the single permitted repair call. Therefore the study does not measure effects due to prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or sampling variation.

Model, validator, and execution constraints. The declared provider/model is gpt‑5‑mini (openai_responses); execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset (this is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a deterministic digital‑twin emulator enforcing manifest workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returning a binary safe‑deploy verdict per episode. The preregistration fixed deterministic seeds, task selection rules, retry limits, and missingness treatments (primary analysis uses complete_pair_primary).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026‑09‑01 and completed as recorded in the execution manifest. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5. All deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The paired contingency table is n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and exploratory analyses. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) computed post‑hoc yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 it is reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not affect the preregistered confirmatory inference. Representative archived episode artifacts show five validator‑triggered repairs where the validator rejected an initial candidate for required_sequence or protected_interface violations, an allowed single repair call was invoked, and the repaired candidate passed revalidation. Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5).

Why the bootstrap CI can exclude zero while the preregistered McNemar is non‑significant. With extremely sparse discordant counts (n10 + n01 = 5), exact discrete paired tests produce stepwise p‑value behavior: here the two‑sided exact McNemar p = 0.0625. Bootstrap percentile intervals computed on resampled paired outcomes can produce percentile bounds that exclude zero even when an exact test does not reject because resampling approximates the sampling distribution under the observed marginal structure and can overweight rare discordant resamples; the bootstrap CI in this study is therefore a preregistered descriptive summary sensitive to sparse discordant counts. The confirmatory inferential claim follows the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (p = 0.0625); the bootstrap CI and any post‑hoc one‑sided test are explicitly labeled and interpreted as descriptive or exploratory artifacts, respectively.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive outcomes. The preregistered primary inference (exact two‑sided McNemar) did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625) and therefore the preregistered H1 is not supported. Secondary and exploratory summaries indicate a small absolute guarded benefit but are limited by the extreme baseline success rate and sparse discordant counts. We emphasize the inferential primacy of the preregistered two‑sided McNemar test and present the bootstrap CI only as a descriptive diagnostic that must be interpreted with caution in this regime.

Mechanistic implications under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because initial candidates were shared, observed paired gains (n10 = 5) reflect only downstream validator and repair activity. The five repairs illustrate that a deterministic validator with suitable rule coverage can correct certain ordering and protected‑field violations. The low repair count may reflect (a) relatively few initial candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, (b) the sampled model+prompt producing mostly valid candidates, or (c) validator rule coverage that admits some semantic errors. Differentiating these causes requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates downstream effects but precludes measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity: the synthetic stress corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini) restrict generalizability to heterogeneous production environments and other model families. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline produces few discordant pairs and reduces power for exact paired tests relative to the preregistered power assumption (baseline≈0.60).

Recommended preregistered follow‑ups. (1) Run an independent first‑pass generation arm (no shared_initial_candidate) to evaluate prompt/decoding interventions. (2) Sweep repair budgets beyond one permitted repair to estimate marginal returns by failure class. (3) Expand validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity. (4) Evaluate multiple model families to assess model dependence. All follow‑ups should be preregistered with power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The confirmatory inference follows the preregistered McNemar result; bootstrap and post‑hoc one‑sided summaries are presented as descriptive/exploratory diagnostics. Artifact‑grounded traces and manifests are archived to enable reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model, validator, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
